question: An auditorium with \(20\) rows of seats has \(10\) seats in the first row. Each successive row has one more seat than the previous row. If students taking an exam are permitted to sit in any row, but not next to another student in that row, then the maximum number of students that can be seated for an exam is
solution:
To bound the number of students in a row, group its seats into adjacent pairs. Each pair holds at most one student. An even-length row is entirely paired; an odd-length row has one extra end seat that can hold one more student. Occupying every other seat, starting with the first, attains these bounds.

The \(20\) rows have \(10,11,\ldots,29\) seats. Group consecutive rows as
\[
(10,11),\ (12,13),\ \ldots,\ (28,29).
\]
Their maximum student counts are respectively
\[
5+6=11,\quad6+7=13,\quad\ldots,\quad14+15=29.
\]
Thus the total maximum is \(11+13+\cdots+29\). Pairing the first and last terms gives \(11+29=40\), the next pair gives \(13+27=40\), and so on. There are five such pairs, giving
\[
5\times40=200.
\]
Because the restriction applies only within each row, all these row maxima can be attained together. The answer is \(\boxed{200}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).

solutionMethods.explanation:
If a row holds \(s\) students, there are \(s-1\) gaps between consecutive students. Each gap needs at least one empty seat, so at least
\[
s+(s-1)=2s-1
\]
seats are required. Alternating occupied and empty seats achieves this minimum.

For example, five students need at least nine seats, six need eleven seats, and each additional student requires two more seats. Consequently, the maximum occupancies of the rows with \(10\) through \(29\) seats are
\[
5,6,6,7,7,\ldots,14,14,15.
\]
The first and last values occur once, and each value from \(6\) through \(14\) occurs twice. Their sum is
\[
(5+15)+2(6+7+\cdots+14).
\]
In the inner sum, \(6+14\), \(7+13\), \(8+12\), and \(9+11\) each equal \(20\), with \(10\) left over. Thus the total is
\[
20+2(4\times20+10)=200.
\]
Alternating seats in every row realizes this total, so the maximum is \(\boxed{200}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
solutionMethods.label: Count the empty gaps
